notes: Continued from Week 1

This Week 2 introduction continues pretend cooking in Dramatic Play, adding recipes, cookbooks and pretend spices. Use the physical props listed below; the companion illustration is not a photograph of this class.
Vocabulary
chop: cut into small pieces
ingredients: things that are mixed together to make a dish
peel: to take off the skin from a fruit or vegetable
prepare: to make something
recipe: a list of ingredients and directions for making food
stir: to mix by moving a spoon/ladle in a circle
Additional Materials
Soup Day, Melissa Iwai. Flag the recipe at the end of the book.
recipes or cookbooks. Flag pages with soup recipes.
pretend spices or empty spice containers or something to represent spice containers
spice labels (to add to empty containers or taped to blocks)
Preparation
Bring the following to the Intro to Centers: Soup Day, a pot, a ladle, a few spices.
Intro to Centers
Did you visit Dramatic Play last week? Remember all of the different kinds of soup we made?
Invite a few children to share their experiences in the Center so far.

This week, we will continue to be chefs in the kitchen making different kinds of soup. This week, I added a few soup recipes and cookbooks for you to reference. Remember that a recipe includes ingredients and directions to follow to cook something. There is a recipe at the end of Soup Day!
Show the recipe in Soup Day. Point to the ingredients list and the directions. Read aloud.
You and a friend might work together to make Vegetable Soup when you visit Dramatic Play.

I also added a few new spices to Dramatic Play such as salt and pepper. These spices help to change the flavor of food. You might want to use these spices in your soup, as well. You don’t need a lot, just a little bit to adjust the taste of your soup.
Show the spices. Demonstrate adding some salt and pepper to a pot.
Standards
SEL7: The child will demonstrate the ability to communicate with others in a variety of ways.
SEL8: The child will engage socially, and build relationships with other children and with adults.
APL5: The child will cooperate with others in play and learning.
SL.PK.1. Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners during daily routines and play.

title: Storytelling with Props
lead: In Library and Listening this week, you can retell this story, or tell the story again.
alt: Original beginning of Strictly No Elephants showing the boy and his tiny pet elephant.
notes: Purpose
Children use book character puppets and props to retell Strictly No Elephants.
Big Ideas
We can all communicate about colors.
There is an infinite variety of colors.
Guiding Questions
What colors do we notice all around us?
How can we explore and communicate ideas and feelings through colors?
How do colors provide information?
Family Engagement

Continue to invite families and caregivers to share their children’s favorite books/stories to retell in the Library and Listening Center. If families share titles of stories, share the story electronically or find the title at the library.
Vocabulary
character: a person or animal in a story, play, or movie
retell: to tell a story again
Materials and Preparation
Strictly No Elephants, Lisa Mantchev
Strictly No Elephants character puppets (included with Read Aloud plans)
small basket or container to hold character puppets
large fabric swatches
additional props such as stuffed animals, animal figurines, an umbrella
white paper
writing and drawing tools
glue sticks or tape, to make additional puppets/props
popsicle sticks, to make additional puppets/props
scissors, to make additional puppets/props
Bring the following to the Intro to Centers: Strictly No Elephants, character puppets, 1 fabric swatch, additional props
Intro to Centers
We enjoyed reading Strictly No Elephants. In Library and Listening this week, you can retell this story, or tell the story again.
Show Strictly No Elephants.
To help you retell the story, the character puppets will be in Library and Listening.

Show the character puppets. Open to the beginning of Strictly No Elephants and invite children to describe the scene and narrate what is happening. Demonstrate using the puppet(s) to act out the scene, using vocabulary and dialogue.
I also added some more items to the Center. You will find fabric swatches and a few additional props. You might decide to also use these items to help you retell the story.
Show fabric and props.
During Centers

Children retell the story using the character puppets and/or the props. Support children to negotiate choosing puppets/props. A child without a puppet might be the narrator who turns the pages of the book to help the actors retell the story.
Children might want to create additional props such as the “Strictly No Elephants sign” or pet puppets.
Affirm children’s impulses to change the story in original ways.
Differentiation Ideas

Turn the pages of the book to help children remember one story event at a time; talk through what’s happening in the illustration and/or reread the text; make suggestions about what a character can say.
Use story sequencing visuals from the visual comprehension resource included in the differentiated access for each read aloud.
Invite children to draw a character or an event in a story.
Invite children to retell an alternate ending or add characters.
Facilitation
What happens in this book?
What is happening here with the characters, the people or animals in the story?
How do you think the character feels during this part?
Has something like this ever happened to you? Tell us about what happened.
How might you tell a different ending to the story?
Extensions
Invite children to retell additional favorite books from home or teachers’ favorite books.
Standards
SEL5. The child will display empathetic characteristics.
APL5. The child will cooperate with others in play and learning.
APL8. The child will be able to retain and recall information.
RL.PK.2. With prompting and support, retell a sequence of events from a story read aloud.
